title: What are Interfaces?
overview: Interfaces in TypeScript define the structure of an object. They describe what properties and methods an object should contain.

example.title: Interface Example

title: Creating an Interface
overview: An interface is created using the interface keyword followed by the interface name and object structure.

example.title: Create Interface

title: Using Interfaces with Objects
overview: Interfaces can be used to define the type of objects. Objects must follow the structure defined by the interface.

example.title: Object with Interface

title: Optional Properties in Interfaces
overview: Interface properties can be optional by adding a question mark. Optional properties do not need to be provided when creating an object.

title: Readonly Properties
overview: Readonly properties cannot be modified after the object is created. They are useful for values that should remain unchanged.

title: Interfaces in React Native
overview: Interfaces are commonly used in React Native to define component props, API responses, navigation parameters, and application data structures.

example.title: Component Props Example

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how interfaces define object structures, optional properties, readonly properties, and their usage in React Native applications.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:

✔ They improve type safety.
